7426.content: The NAVSTAR GPS architecture combined the Navy's medium-Earth-orbit satellites and spaceborne clocks with the Air Force's pseudorandom-code ranging. Although often expanded as if it were an acronym, NAVSTAR was the program name applied to the unified satellite-navigation system rather than a technical description of one component.

7432.title: Navigation
7432.heading: Navigation
7432.content:
Navigation combines the motor and cognitive work of moving through an environment. Its motor component is [[3D Travel]], and its cognitive component is [[Wayfinding]].

Travel changes the viewpoint or location. Wayfinding determines where to go and how to get there. An efficient travel method is insufficient when the user lacks the [[Spatial Knowledge]] needed to choose a route, while a good route plan is useless without a controllable way to move.

Designers can integrate the two through maps, landmarks, view overviews, or techniques that reinforce a [[Cognitive Map]] while the user travels.

AR can support navigation in the traveler's own physical frame by registering points of interest, routes, and directional cues with the visible environment. A [[Multiple-Perspective Interface]] can connect this local guidance to an overview when the user also needs global route structure.

7435.title: Navigation Mesh
7435.heading: Navigation Mesh
7435.content:
A navigation mesh partitions walkable space into connected convex polygons. An agent can move directly within one polygon and search adjacency between polygons to plan a route through the environment.

Compared with isolated [[Path Node|path nodes]], the mesh describes traversable regions rather than only preferred points. It supports more flexible movement while still reducing detailed world geometry to a manageable [[Pathfinding Graph]].

A nature-derived color scheme samples relationships already observed in landscapes, plants, animals, weather, or other real scenes. Such references can provide a coherent starting palette without requiring the artist to begin from a formal wheel construction.

The sampled colors still need adjustment for the game's lighting, mood, and readability. Their relative hue, saturation, and value matter more than copying isolated swatches, and controlled contrast may be added to guide player attention.

7441.title: Natural Number
7441.heading: Natural Number
7441.content:
A natural number is a member of the ordered collection

$$\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,3,\ldots\}.$$

Natural numbers are used to count objects and identify positions in an order. Addition and multiplication of two natural numbers produce another natural number, so these operations satisfy the [[Closure Property]] on this set. Subtraction and division can leave it: (3-5) is not natural, and neither is (3/5). Extending natural numbers with opposites produces the [[Integer]]s.

Natural language understanding converts a word sequence into a symbolic representation an assistant can act on. It tries to identify the user's [[Intent]], the relevant [[Entity|entities]], and the relationships among them.

NLU operates after [[Automatic Speech Recognition]] in a spoken assistant. A correct transcript can still be misunderstood, because recognizing words and interpreting their purpose are different problems.

Natural language generation converts a symbolic response into words suitable for the user and situation. It decides what information to express, how to organize it, and which linguistic form to use.

A typical pipeline includes a [[Sentence Planner]], [[Microplanner]], and [[Lexicalization]] stage. The resulting text can be displayed or passed to [[Text-to-Speech]] for spoken delivery.

7450.heading: Natural Information Processes
7450.content:
A natural information process is a phenomenon interpreted through states, representations, transformations, and exchanges of information. Examples include biological regulation, cognitive activity, and physical interactions modeled computationally.

Such an interpretation is valuable when it yields testable explanations or productive simulations. The meaning of the represented information remains tied to the scientific domain rather than supplied by the computer.

7453.title: Natural Frequency
7453.heading: Natural Frequency
7453.content:
A natural frequency is a rate at which a structure can vibrate freely after disturbance. It is obtained from the nontrivial solutions of the stiffness-mass eigenvalue equation and is commonly reported in radians per second or hertz.

Geometry, stiffness, material density, and boundary conditions determine the values. Mesh refinement improves the finite element approximation, especially for higher frequencies.

7456.heading: Natural Feature Tracking
7456.content:
Natural feature tracking estimates pose from distinctive image structure already present in the environment instead of requiring artificial markers. Interest points are detected, described, and matched to a prepared model or to features observed in earlier frames.

The method allows less intrusive AR, but feature quality changes with viewpoint, scale, illumination, blur, and occlusion. Robust pose estimation must separate geometrically consistent matches from false correspondences.

Since its breaks depend on a particular dataset, two maps may use different numeric meanings for the same colors. Shared breaks are necessary when maps must be compared directly.

7462.title: Natural and Forced Convection
7462.heading: Natural and Forced Convection
7462.content:
Natural convection arises when temperature-dependent density differences create buoyant motion without a fan or pump. Warm fluid tends to rise and cooler, denser fluid tends to descend, forming circulation that enhances heat exchange near a surface.

Forced convection uses mechanical motion to drive the fluid and can raise the effective [[Convective Heat Transfer Coefficient|convection coefficient]] substantially. A boundary-coefficient model may represent either regime, while a [[Buoyancy-Driven Thermal Flow|coupled flow model]] resolves the motion explicitly.

A native web application combines multiple small single-page modules within a multipage web structure. It uses browser and server navigation where appropriate instead of forcing every capability into one long-lived client application.

This hybrid arrangement can preserve SPA-like interactive sections while allowing selected page transitions, redirects, or services to operate independently. It therefore differs from a single, fully client-routed [[Single-Page Application]].

A native mobile application is implemented with the language, SDK, controls, and runtime conventions of its target operating system. It offers direct access to platform APIs and generally the clearest path to platform-specific performance and user experience.

The tradeoff is duplication across targets: an iOS and an Android edition may require different skills, codebases, and maintenance work even when they implement the same product behavior.

The shared layer reduces repeated business and interface code without requiring every platform difference to disappear.

Each target still has an application head or harness for startup, packaging, permissions, and native integrations. Xamarin and Xamarin.Forms apply this model with shared .NET code and platform-specific projects.

7477.heading: Narrative Synthesis with Traceability
7477.content:
Narrative synthesis assembles selected text units into a larger storyline rather than only breaking a story apart for analysis. The book proposes controlling the target length, using mapped transitions to make adjoining passages coherent, and retaining a route back to each component text.

That traceability can matter for revision, interactive branches, and attribution or digital rights. A geometric or hierarchical support tool can suggest structure, but authors still judge whether the assembled sequence carries an intelligible dramatic meaning for its audience.

7480.title: Narrative Style Randomization
7480.heading: Narrative Style Randomization
7480.content:
Randomizing the order of narrative units supplies a comparison for observed tempo, rhythm, and movement through a semantic factor space. The book analyzes Casablanca scenes and beats against repeated reordered alternatives rather than declaring every visual pattern distinctive by inspection.

The test depends on what is randomized and which style statistic is measured. A result unusual under shuffled order says that sequence matters for that statistic; it does not establish the aesthetic quality or causal meaning of the story by itself.

7483.title: Narrative Interpretation
7483.heading: Narrative Interpretation
7483.content:
Narrative interpretation is the audience's construction of meaning from arranged events, images, rules, and omissions. A story comes into being not only through what its author provides, but through the connections a player makes while experiencing it.

Games make this process especially visible because players act inside the system and may encounter different fragments. Even when mechanics remain fixed, different players can understand what those mechanics express in different ways.

7486.title: Narrative Episodization
7486.heading: Narrative Episodization
7486.content:
Episodization divides a larger narrative into meaningful, ordered passages before analyzing or composing it. The book applies semantic maps and sequence-constrained hierarchies to scenes, sub-scenes, and tweet segments, using changes between adjacent passages to propose where one episode gives way to another.

For interactive or cross-platform stories, such segmentation can support authoring decisions without dictating a single plot. The level of resolution matters: a scene, dramatic beat, tweet, or text block exposes different kinds of transition and different degrees of audience interpretation.

7489.title: Narrative Ambiguity
7489.heading: Narrative Ambiguity
7489.content:
Narrative ambiguity leaves events, motives, relationships, or meanings partly unresolved so the audience must interpret them. In games, ambiguity can also result from hidden systems and from players discovering different amounts of authored material.

Ambiguity opens space for several plausible understandings rather than supplying one final explanation. It is most productive when the available evidence supports interpretation, not when essential information is missing by accident.

7498.sourceSearchName: nakayama s lemma nakayama s lemma
7498.title: Nakayama's Lemma
7498.heading: Nakayama's Lemma
7498.content:
Nakayama's lemma states that if M is a finitely generated module and I lies in the [[Jacobson Radical]], then IM = M implies M = 0. More generally, M = IM + N implies M = N.

Over a [[Local Ring]], a basis of M/mM over the [[Residue Field]] lifts to a minimal generating set of M. The lemma converts information after reduction modulo the maximal ideal into information about the original module.

7501.title: Naive Bayes Sensor Fusion
7501.heading: Naive Bayes Sensor Fusion
7501.content:
Naive Bayes sensor fusion estimates a hidden state from several readings by assuming the sensors are conditionally independent once that state is known. The joint model factors into a state prior multiplied by one sensor model for each reading.

This sharply reduces dimensionality and makes additional sensors easy to incorporate. The assumption is only an approximation when unmodeled causes correlate the readings, so its computational benefit must be weighed against the quality required by the task.

7504.sourceSearchName: naive bayes conditional independence naive bayes conditional independence
7504.title: Naive Bayes Conditional Independence
7504.heading: Naive Bayes Conditional Independence
7504.content:
Naive Bayes conditional independence assumes that observed features are mutually independent once the class label is known. The joint class-conditional likelihood can therefore be written as a product of separate feature likelihoods.

The assumption is deliberately strong and often false in literal terms, yet it turns a high-dimensional density estimate into tractable counts or parameter estimates. Prediction compares each class prior multiplied by its featurewise evidence.

7507.title: Naive Bayes Classifier
7507.heading: Naive Bayes Classifier
7507.content:
A naive Bayes classifier estimates a class score by multiplying the class prior by the conditional likelihood of each observed feature under that class. It predicts the class with the largest posterior-proportional product.

The method assumes the features are conditionally independent given the class. This strong simplification makes training and classification efficient; smoothing is needed when an unseen feature-class combination would otherwise give a zero product.

7510.heading: N-Type Semiconductor

Electrons can be promoted from these levels into available conduction states at ordinary temperatures, making electrons its main mobile carriers. Paired with a [[P-Type Semiconductor]], it forms a [[P-N Junction]] whose field can separate light-generated carriers. The impurity amount affects conductivity.

7513.content:
An n-gram language model estimates the probability of a word from a fixed number of preceding words. Counts in a text corpus provide probabilities for recurring sequences such as unigrams, bigrams, or trigrams.

Its limited history makes computation manageable during [[Speech Recognition Search]], but it cannot directly preserve distant context. Smoothing is needed when a plausible sequence was rare or absent in the training text.

Dapper multi-mapping or multiple result sets can gather parent and child data in fewer trips. The replacement should still be measured because a single oversized query can introduce different costs.

A muscle-powered robot attaches living contractile tissue to a skeleton whose geometry directs the resulting force. Asymmetry can turn equal contractions into crawling, while films, tails, fins, or tubes create pumping and swimming motions.

Performance depends on tissue strength, stimulation, attachment, skeleton stiffness, friction, fluid mechanics, and the health of the culture environment.

7537.heading: Muscle-on-a-Chip
7537.content:
A muscle-on-a-chip forms engineered muscle between flexible anchors or pillars. Electrical stimulation causes contraction, and measured pillar deflection can be converted into force using the pillar's known geometry and material properties.

Cells carrying a disease-associated mutation let the platform compare contractility and screen compounds intended to restore muscle function.

7540.title: Muscle Tetanus
7540.heading: Muscle Tetanus
7540.content:
Muscle tetanus is sustained contraction produced when stimuli arrive so rapidly that the tissue cannot relax between them. Individual twitches merge into a stable force while high-frequency stimulation continues.

Biohybrid devices can use tetanus to hold a grip or position, but prolonged activation increases fatigue and should not be confused with the infectious disease also called tetanus.

7543.title: Multiview Triangulation
7543.heading: Multiview Triangulation
7543.content:
Multiview triangulation reconstructs a three-dimensional point from corresponding image observations in two or more calibrated cameras. Each observation defines a viewing ray, and the desired point is estimated where those rays meet most consistently.

Noise and calibration error usually prevent an exact intersection. Additional views can supply redundancy, but the result still depends on correct correspondence and camera geometry with a useful baseline.

7546.heading: Multivariate Polynomial Division
7546.content:
Multivariate polynomial division reduces a polynomial by an ordered list of divisors using a fixed [[Monomial Order]]. At each step, a divisible leading term is cancelled; otherwise that term is moved to the remainder.

Unlike one-variable division, the remainder can depend on divisor order unless the divisors form a [[Gröbner Basis]]. A Gröbner basis makes zero remainder a reliable test for ideal membership.

7561.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions
7561.heading: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions
7561.content:
Rational expressions multiply by multiplying numerators and denominators. Factoring first allows common factors to be cancelled across the product. Division by a nonzero rational expression changes to multiplication by its [[Reciprocal]].

For each operation, every original denominator must be nonzero, and a divisor must also have a nonzero numerator so that its reciprocal is defined. Cancelling before expansion usually keeps the calculation smaller. The final expression should be stated together with the restrictions inherited from the original forms.

7564.heading: Multiplicity of a Graded Module
7564.content:
For a non-Artinian finitely generated graded module M of dimension d, its multiplicity is obtained from the leading coefficient of its [[Hilbert Polynomial]] after multiplying by (d−1)!.

Multiplicity measures the leading rate of graded growth rather than the full Hilbert function. The associative formula decomposes it into contributions from top-dimensional prime components.

7567.sourceSearchName: multiplicatively closed set multiplicatively closed set
7567.title: Multiplicatively Closed Set
7567.heading: Multiplicatively Closed Set
7567.content:
A multiplicatively closed set S contains the [[Ring Identity]] and is closed under multiplication. It specifies which elements may appear as denominators in [[Ring Localization]].

If an ideal is disjoint from S, a maximality argument produces a [[Prime Ideal]] containing that ideal and still disjoint from S. Primes that meet S disappear after localization because one of their elements becomes invertible.

7568.title: Multiplicatively Closed Set
7568.heading: References

7570.title: Multiplicative Inverse
7570.heading: Multiplicative Inverse
7570.content:
A multiplicative inverse of an element a is an element u for which au equals the [[Ring Identity]]. When it exists, a is a [[Ring Unit]] and the inverse is written a⁻¹.

Every nonzero element of a [[Field]] has an inverse. A general [[Commutative Ring]] can contain nonzero elements without inverses, which is why localization changes a ring by formally adjoining selected inverses.

7572.sourceSearchName: multiplication property of inequality multiplication property of inequality
7572.title: Multiplication Property of Inequality
7572.heading: Document

7573.sourceSearchName: multiplication property of inequality multiplication property of inequality
7573.title: Multiplication Property of Inequality
7573.heading: Multiplication Property of Inequality
7573.content:
The multiplication property of inequality depends on the sign of the common multiplier. If (a<b) and (c>0), then

$$ac<bc.$$

Multiplication by a positive value scales both positions without changing their order. If (c<0), the order reverses:

$$ac>bc.$$

Division follows the same rule because it multiplies by a reciprocal. This sign-sensitive behavior is the key difference between solving inequalities and solving equations.

7574.sourceSearchName: multiplication property of inequality multiplication property of inequality
7574.title: Multiplication Property of Inequality
7574.heading: References

7575.sourceSearchName: multiplication property of equality multiplication property of equality
7575.title: Multiplication Property of Equality
7575.heading: Document

7576.sourceSearchName: multiplication property of equality multiplication property of equality
7576.title: Multiplication Property of Equality
7576.heading: Multiplication Property of Equality
7576.content:
The multiplication property of equality states that multiplying equal quantities by the same number preserves equality. If (a=b), then

$$ac=bc.$$

Division by the same nonzero number is the inverse use of this property. The nonzero restriction is essential when reversing the transformation, because multiplication by zero collapses every value to the same equation. The property isolates coefficients, clears denominators, and creates [[Equivalent Equations]] during solving.

7577.sourceSearchName: multiplication property of equality multiplication property of equality
7577.title: Multiplication Property of Equality
7577.heading: References

7579.title: Multiplex Network
7579.heading: Multiplex Network
7579.content:
A multiplex network contains several edge layers defined over exactly the same set of nodes. Each layer may be directed or undirected and weighted or unweighted, but every entity has a corresponding presence in every layer.

The layers can represent different forms of interaction among the same people or components. Identity connections tie a node's copies together without erasing the distinction between relationship types.

7591.heading: Multiple Testing Problem
7591.content:
The multiple testing problem arises when many hypotheses are examined simultaneously. Even if every null hypothesis is true, applying the same per-test p-value cutoff repeatedly can produce one or more false positives with high probability.

High-throughput inference therefore defines a selection procedure and controls an error rate for the resulting list. [[Family-Wise Error Rate]] and [[False Discovery Rate]] express different tolerances for mistakes and lead to different discovery power.

7597.heading: Multiplayer Distributed Gaming
7597.content:
Multiplayer distributed gaming places players at separate machines connected through a network. Each participant can receive an individual view and private information, unlike local multiplayer on one shared display.

Distribution expands possible scale and distance while adding synchronization and trust problems. The software must decide which machine or server is authoritative and how inconsistent views are reconciled.

7600.title: Multiplayer Complexity
7600.heading: Multiplayer Complexity
7600.content:
Multiplayer complexity is the uncertainty and strategic richness created when several human minds act within the same game system. Players do not merely respond to rules; they anticipate, surprise, cooperate with, and communicate through actions to one another.

A simple system may remain predictable even with two people, but strongly interacting choices can produce distinctive [[Emergent Story|emergent stories]]. Human intentions make the possibility space difficult to reproduce with fixed computer behavior alone.

7603.title: Multiparty System
7603.heading: Multiparty System
7603.content:
A multiparty system allows several political parties to compete for and hold legislative seats. No organization may control an absolute majority, so governing, opposition, and minority groups depend on negotiation and shifting coalitions.

Network interpretations developed for two-party legislatures may not transfer directly. Party weakness, electoral rules, executive power, and low re-election can change what co-sponsorship and switching mean.

7606.sourceSearchName: multinomial text classification model multinomial text classification model
7606.title: Multinomial Text Classification Model
7606.heading: Multinomial Text Classification Model
7606.content:
A multinomial text classification model treats a document as counts of word draws from a class-specific vocabulary distribution. Repeated occurrences therefore contribute repeated evidence to the class likelihood.

Training estimates each class's term probabilities, normally with smoothing to handle unseen words. Document length influences the number of draws, while the relative frequencies distinguish categories with different characteristic vocabularies.

7609.title: Multimodal Interaction
7609.heading: Multimodal Interaction
7609.content:
Multimodal interaction combines multiple input or output channels in one interface. A person may switch between modalities or use them together, such as speaking a command while pointing to its spatial arguments.

Multiple channels can decouple [[System Control]] from a primary task, resolve ambiguous speech or gestures, support complementary strengths, and give users alternatives when one channel is blocked. They can also increase [[Cognitive Load]] or disrupt the flow of action if switching and coordination are poorly designed.

The task should be matched to suitable modalities, transitions should be clear, and combined performance should be evaluated rather than assumed to improve automatically.

In a virtual assistant, speech can be combined with a display, touch, gaze, or physical orientation. The [[Dialog Manager]] must keep these channels in one [[Conversation Context]] so expressions such as “that one” can be resolved against what the user sees or indicates.

An AR interface can combine speech with [[Gesture Interaction|gesture]], touch, tracked objects, gaze, and haptic output in the same physical frame. One modality can disambiguate another—for example, a spoken command can name an operation while a pointing gesture identifies the situated object to which it applies.

7611.title: Multimodal Data Clustering

7612.heading: Multimodal Data Clustering
7612.content:
Multimodal clustering combines representations from sources such as text, imagery, audio, and video. Fusion may occur before clustering through a joint feature space or during clustering through coupled objectives and multiple similarity graphs.

Early fusion is simple but vulnerable to incompatible scales and missing modalities. Model-level fusion can weight evidence separately, though it introduces more parameters and must distinguish complementary signals from redundant or conflicting ones.

7615.heading: Multimedia Feature Extraction
7615.content:
Multimedia feature extraction converts raw text, images, audio, or video into numerical descriptions that a classifier can compare. Image color and texture, acoustic measurements, motion, and accompanying words expose different aspects of the same item.

Preprocessing must respect the modality's scale and temporal or spatial structure. A classifier cannot recover distinctions that the extracted representation discarded, so feature design is part of the predictive model.

7618.title: Multilevel Network
7618.heading: Multilevel Network
7618.content:
A multilevel network organizes a graph as a family of subgraphs whose node and edge unions form the complete system. Each level can represent a distinct scale or grouping while remaining part of one overall network.

The formulation emphasizes nested or grouped structure rather than requiring identical node sets across layers. Analysis can compare within-level patterns with relationships that span levels.

7621.title: Multilevel Graph Partitioning
7621.heading: Multilevel Graph Partitioning
7621.content:
Multilevel graph partitioning repeatedly contracts vertices or edges to create a hierarchy of smaller graphs, partitions the coarsest graph, and then projects and refines the solution while uncoarsening.

Coarsening makes a global cut problem manageable and can reveal large-scale structure before local details. Contraction must preserve important connectivity, and refinement is needed because coarse decisions create boundary errors at finer levels.

7624.title: Multilayer Perceptron
7624.heading: Multilayer Perceptron
7624.content:
A multilayer perceptron contains an input layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer with weighted connections between adjacent layers. Nonlinear activations let the network represent relationships that are not linearly separable.

Feedforward computation produces predictions, while backpropagation and gradient descent adjust weights to reduce an error function.

Kelleher uses the transition from one-layer [[Perceptron|perceptrons]] to multilayer networks to explain the importance of hidden-unit credit assignment. [[Backpropagation]] can train those hidden weights when the network has activation functions with usable derivatives. Nonlinear layers overcome the one-line boundary limit illustrated by [[XOR Classification Problem|XOR]], though deep stacks also raise the [[Vanishing Gradient Problem|vanishing-gradient]] challenge.

7627.title: Multilayer Network
7627.heading: Multilayer Network
7627.content:
A multilayer network represents a connected system with several network layers and relationships within or across them. Nodes may appear in one or more layers, and interlayer edges preserve dependencies that a collection of isolated graphs would omit.

Different constraints produce multiplex, interdependent, interconnected, temporal, and other network types. The representation matters because aggregation can change paths, centrality, diffusion, and failure behavior.

7629.sourceSearchName: multilayer network synchronization multilayer network synchronization
7629.title: Multilayer Network Synchronization
7629.heading: Document

7630.sourceSearchName: multilayer network synchronization multilayer network synchronization
7630.title: Multilayer Network Synchronization
7630.heading: Multilayer Network Synchronization
7630.content:
Multilayer network synchronization is the coordination of dynamic states across connected layers. Coupling within and between networks determines whether initially different processes converge, remain separated, or destabilize one another.

A supra-adjacency or related spectral representation can expose how interlayer strength changes synchronizability. The complete multilayer structure matters because layer aggregation may predict different behavior.

7631.sourceSearchName: multilayer network synchronization multilayer network synchronization
7631.title: Multilayer Network Synchronization
7631.heading: References

7632.sourceSearchName: multilayer network aggregation multilayer network aggregation
7632.title: Multilayer Network Aggregation
7632.heading: Document

7633.sourceSearchName: multilayer network aggregation multilayer network aggregation
7633.title: Multilayer Network Aggregation
7633.heading: Multilayer Network Aggregation
7633.content:
Multilayer network aggregation combines several layers into a simpler graph, often by merging corresponding nodes and treating any layer edge as a connection. The result reduces computational and visual complexity.

Aggregation can change degrees, paths, communities, and dynamic processes because it erases edge types and layer constraints. It should therefore be justified by the question rather than used as a neutral preprocessing step.

7634.sourceSearchName: multilayer network aggregation multilayer network aggregation
7634.title: Multilayer Network Aggregation
7634.heading: References

7636.title: Multilayer Diffusion
7636.heading: Multilayer Diffusion
7636.content:
Multilayer diffusion spreads information, behavior, disease, or failure through within-layer and interlayer connections. Participation in several networks creates routes unavailable in any one layer.

Threshold, cascade, and epidemic models can be extended to this setting, but their behavior may change because exposures and dependencies cross layer boundaries. Aggregating layers can conceal those mechanisms.

7642.title: Multigraph
7642.heading: Multigraph
7642.content:
A multigraph is a [[Graph]] that permits multiple instances of an edge between the same pair of vertices. The repeated edges are distinct relationships even though their endpoints are identical.

The Königsberg bridge representation is a multigraph because several separate bridges connect the same landmasses. Preserving those parallel edges is essential when the question asks whether every physical bridge can be crossed exactly once.

7645.title: Multidimensional Scaling
7645.heading: Multidimensional Scaling
7645.content:
Multidimensional scaling constructs low-dimensional coordinates whose pairwise distances approximate an input [[Distance Matrix]]. A two-dimensional scaling plot makes relative similarity among high-dimensional samples visible without plotting every original feature.

For Euclidean distances, the source relates the leading scaling coordinates to the leading singular-vector representation. The plot is most faithful when the first few dimensions dominate the distance structure.

7648.title: Multidimensional Network
7648.heading: Multidimensional Network
7648.content:
A multidimensional network assigns a label or dimension to each edge. The same pair of nodes can have several connections as long as each belongs to a different dimension.

Mapping every edge label to a [[Network Layer]] turns the structure into a multiplex representation. The dimensions preserve interaction types that would otherwise become one aggregated tie.

7651.sourceSearchName: multidimensional dynamic time warping multidimensional dynamic time warping
7651.title: Multidimensional Dynamic Time Warping
7651.heading: Multidimensional Dynamic Time Warping
7651.content:
Multidimensional dynamic time warping aligns two vector-valued sequences by finding a low-cost path through their pairwise temporal positions. The path permits local stretching and compression while preserving order.

A joint local cost keeps the dimensions synchronized during alignment, unlike warping each coordinate independently. Constraints on the path reduce computation and prevent implausible matches that align distant events solely to lower numerical cost.

7654.title: Multidimensional Database
7654.heading: Multidimensional Database
7654.content:
A multidimensional database organizes measures across dimensions so users can examine data from several perspectives. Its structure supports rapid aggregation and navigation through categories, time periods, locations, or other analytic axes.

Data cubes and online analytical processing expose these dimensions through operations such as pivoting, filtering, drilling, and slicing. The representation is especially useful during exploratory analysis.

7657.content:
Multicluster feature selection uses several spectral directions to represent multiple latent groups rather than scoring features against a single division. A sparse regression or related selection step identifies features that jointly explain those directions.

Using multiple directions helps preserve distinctions among several clusters and can capture complementary features. The estimated number of structural directions and the similarity graph remain modeling choices that affect the selected subset.

7660.heading: Multiconstellation GNSS Receiver
7660.content: A multiconstellation GNSS receiver observes satellites from more than one navigation system, such as GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, or BeiDou. More visible transmitters can improve availability and geometry in urban canyons, at high latitudes, or where part of the sky is blocked. Combining systems requires compatible radio bands, signal processing, coordinate frames, and time-offset handling; the receiver must reconcile those differences rather than simply count satellites.

The physical environment provides a common frame that helps relate the views. Designers must preserve consistency and awareness so actions in one view can be understood from the others.

Multi-view feature selection chooses variables when each object is described by several distinct feature sets or modalities. It must use complementary information across views while controlling redundancy within and between them.

A selector may seek agreement, preserve view-specific structure, or weight views by predictive value. Treating all dimensions as one undifferentiated matrix can obscure these relationships.

7669.title: Multi-Tenancy
7669.heading: Multi-Tenancy
7669.content:
Multi-tenancy is the use of a shared cloud resource or service by multiple consumers. The shared resource may be software, storage, a platform, or virtualized infrastructure, while each consumer experiences an appropriately separated service.

Sharing improves utilization and spreads costs across tenants. It also makes isolation a central requirement: one tenant's activity or data must not improperly affect the availability, confidentiality, or integrity experienced by another.

7672.heading: Multi-Provider Cloud Usage Model
7672.content:
A multi-provider cloud usage model lets an organization obtain services from several providers while a central IT function retains brokerage and oversight. A service that no longer meets a need can be supplemented or replaced by another provider.

The flexibility creates an integration obligation. The central function must connect providers to one another and to business units while reconciling their contracts, identities, data, service levels, and reports.

7675.title: Multi-Provider Cloud Backup
7675.heading: Multi-Provider Cloud Backup
7675.content:
Multi-provider cloud backup keeps recovery copies with a provider different from the one holding the primary cloud data, or distributes backup tiers among several providers. This reduces the chance that one outage, business failure, or account problem removes both production data and its recovery copy.

The services need enough interoperability for automated transfer and restoration. Encryption, credentials, egress time, retention, and the ability to recover without the primary provider should all be tested.
